messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: High error rate calling GCP KMS in us-west2 (latency spikes -> 5xx/timeout). Affected: service-startup signing path and runtime request signing. Investigate immediately.

pagerduty: Paging oncall-dev: Critical KMS latency impacting instance startups and API signing - P1.

oncall-dev: Ack. I'm looking. First pass: are we seeing this across all regions or only us-west2?

alice.nguyen: Confirmed from logs: a bunch of new pod restarts in dedicated clusters in us-west2. Errors are "KMS request timeout after 10s" and a small percentage of 503s. Startup failures because signing didn't complete -> service aborts.

ben.suli: Quick query from one affected host: 
```
$ curl -s -D - -o /dev/null "https://kms.googleapis.com/v1/projects/redwood/locations/us-west2/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/sign:asymmetricSign"
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 14:22:00 GMT

"

chandra.patel: Metrics: KMS client latency p50 jumped from 120ms to 7s, p95 ~ 18s. Request rate same. Auth (IAM) checks look OK. No obvious token expiry.

oncall-dev: Mitigation plan (short list):
1) Stop any rolling restarts / new instance onboarding in us-west2 (prevent more startup failures).
2) Enable local cached signing keys / fallback signing for non-sensitive paths (feature flag) to allow existing instances to continue handling traffic.
3) Increase KMS client timeout to 30s and add exponential backoff for retries temporarily.
4) Open case with GCP and attach request traces and sample request/response.
Please ack who can take each item.

alice.nguyen: I'll flip the rollout block -> set env REDWOOD_DISABLE_AUTO_ROLLOUT=true for us-west2 infra pools. Pushing CI job now.

ben.suli: I'll patch runtime to set KMS_SIGNING_TIMEOUT=30000 and KMS_RETRY_BACKOFF=exponential, push hotfix to canary only (no full rollout). Commands for ops: 
```
kubectl set env deployment/infra-runtime REDWOOD_DISABLE_AUTO_ROLLOUT=true -n infra-us-west2
kubectl set env deployment/infra-runtime KMS_SIGNING_TIMEOUT=30000 KMS_RETRY_BACKOFF=exponential -n infra-us-west2
```

support: Noting customer impact: some Dedicated customers in us-west2 seeing failed onboarding & increased error rates for signing-protected endpoints. Support ticket queue rising. Do we want a public status update?

chandra.patel: Yes, send a controlled status update: describe degraded mode for startups and that existing traffic is being routed with fallback signing where safe. No customer secrets exposed. Draft (short): 
"We are experiencing elevated latency to a third-party key management API in the us-west2 region affecting new instance startups and some signing operations. Engineers have applied temporary fallbacks to reduce impact while we work with the provider. We will post updates every 30 minutes."

oncall-dev: Agree. @support please post that to status.redwood.ai and notify top 10 impacted customers via CSM.

infra-bot: ACTION: Created ticket GCP-INC-92412 with attached traces, sample request IDs, and p95/p99 graphs. Case ID in ticket.

pagerduty: Escalation: GCP assigned engineer ENG-4789. ETA for first response 22 minutes.

alice.nguyen: Hotfix applied to canary in us-west2. Observability: startup failure rate decreased by ~60% for patched canary -> fallback signing + longer timeouts helping.

ben.suli: Rolling patch to the rest of infra-us-west2 now, but will hold if GCP asks to revert.

chandra.patel: Monitoring note: increase in client retries created some queueing on our side (inflight requests higher). We're temporarily enabling stricter circuit-breaker thresholds for KMS calls to avoid cascading failure. Config snippet: 
```
kms_client:
  timeout_ms: 30000
  max_retries: 6
  backoff: exponential
  circuit_breaker:
    error_threshold_percent: 40
    recovery_interval_ms: 60000
```

oncall-dev: Good. Assigning follow-ups: 
- Contacted GCP (ben.suli) -> point of contact ENG-4789.
- Status updates & customer comms (support).
- Postmortem/analysis (alice + chandra).

support: Posted status page update and notified 7 customers on watchlist. No public outage page yet; waiting for confirmation of full mitigation.

sre-bot: Incident timeline event logged: 2026-03-03T14:22:00Z - KMS latency spike detected. Incident ID: INC-20260303-06.

oncall-dev: Update: GCP engineer reports they are seeing a control-plane autoscaling bug in a KMS front-end cluster causing request queueing. They are applying a rolling fix; estimate 45-60 minutes to full recovery. GCP suggests our mitigations are reasonable.

alice.nguyen: Rolling back the rollout-block flag in 10 minutes if metrics stable. Current plan: keep KMS timeout/backoff and circuit-breaker for 2 hours post-recovery, then revert to normal.

ben.suli: We should also add a short-term change to our startup path: if signing fails with KMS timeout during startup, don't abort full process on first failure — queue and retry with backoff up to 6 times before failing node startup. I'll open a PR for this behavior change and backport to the startup image.

support: Customers on watchlist reported reduced impact after fallback. One customer still sees intermittent 502s when deploying new instances. We're offering mitigation guidance (wait for 60m then retry deployments).

oncall-dev: Any more actions? If not, we'll keep monitoring and reconvene on handoff in 1 hour.

alice.nguyen: I'll own the postmortem and include recommendations: local key cache TTL review, startup signing retry policy, circuit-breaker tuning, and adding a provider-failure runbook.

chandra.patel: Also add automated alerting when startup fatal errors spike > 0.5% over 10m so paging triggers faster for this specific class.

pagerduty: Incident downgraded to high once GCP confirms rollfix in progress. Final status pending full recovery verification.

sre-bot: Incident INC-20260303-06: state=monitoring.

oncall-dev: Handoff plan: I'll remain on rotation for the next 30 minutes, then hand to oncall-dev+1. Keep the same incident channel for continuity.

support: Will draft customer-facing RCA after postmortem. Noted.

infra-bot: RESOLUTION: GCP reports fix deployed at 15:04 UTC. Metrics show KMS p95 returned to baseline within 10 minutes. Closing sliding window at 15:20 UTC.

sre-bot: Incident INC-20260303-06: state=resolved. Timeline and actions saved to internal incident tracker.

alice.nguyen: Thanks team. Postmortem owners: alice.nguyen, chandra.patel. Target publish ETA: 72 hours.

ben.suli: I'll follow up with a small runtime change to make startup more resilient (PR opened).

support: Closing customer follow-ups as we confirm recovery.

oncall-dev: Closing this thread. If anything regresses, reopen or create new thread and page.
